intro: You are standing in Alexandria Troas, an ancient city in Çanakkale province, whose life stretches from 310 BC to the 6th century AD. It was founded by Antigonus, one of Alexander's generals, and it grew into one of the largest ancient cities of Anatolia.
history: Antigonus Monophthalmus founded the city in 310 BC in the Troad, and it quickly became one of Rome's most important harbour cities. Emperors came here: Augustus and Hadrian both visited. So did St Paul, passing through on his journeys west. And the scale! Covering some 400 hectares, it was even larger than Ephesus, one of the largest urban fabrics of the Roman world.
structure-5: You are now at the Stadium. Look along this elongated venue: here the foot races and athletic contests were held. Pause and imagine the runners, and the shouts that followed them.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Roman Bath and the Odeon, then the Theatre and the Gymnasium, and finally the City Walls.
facts: Did you know? The city covered roughly 400 hectares, even more than Ephesus, making it one of the largest Roman cities in Anatolia. It was also one of Anatolia's largest ports under Rome, and by ancient report Constantine seriously considered founding his capital here. It was here that Saint Paul dreamed of the man calling 'Come over to Macedonia' — Christianity's crossing into Europe began at this harbour. Today the ruins lie scattered through oak woodland, and the locals call the bath building the 'Honey Palace'.
outro: This brings our journey through Alexandria Troas to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let these ruins keep their quiet for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
